data.name: Euphrosynos
data.gender_notes: Euphrosynos is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word eu (good) and phrosyne (joy or happiness). In Greek mythology, Euphrosyne was a goddess of joy and mirth. The name Euphrosynos carries the meaning “Joy, Happiness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Euphrosynos usually hope their child will grow to embody joy, happiness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name reflecting inner joy and happiness.
data.etymology: Euphrosynos belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joy, Happiness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Euphrosynos total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Euphrosynos the Younger, also known as Euphrosynos of Paphlagonia, was a 5th-century ascetic and monk. He was born in Paphlagonia, which is now part of Turkey. Euphrosynos lived in a cave near the Black Sea and was known for his extreme asceticism and dedication to God. He was revered by both monks and laypeople and is remembered as a patron saint of monks and ascetics.
historical_references.context: Early Christian period, asceticism and monasticism

historical_references.reference: Saint Euphrosynos, also known as Euphrosyne of Polotsk, was a 12th-century Russian Orthodox saint and abbess. She was born in Belarus and became a nun at the Monastery of the Intercession in Polotsk. Euphrosynos was known for her piety, wisdom, and miraculous healing powers. She served as abbess for many years and was canonized by the Russian Orthodox Church.
historical_references.context: Medieval period, Russian Orthodoxy, monasticism and healing
